$comment: Generated by `cargo xtask docs` from mto's settings table; do not edit.
title: mto.toml
description: mto's configuration file: mto's own settings and the formatting settings. mto matches values without regard to case; the values here are spelled as `mto config print` writes them.

root.description: Stop the search upwards for mto.toml files at this file: it is the outermost one read.

blank_lines_between_blocks.description:
The number of blank lines placed between items. Imports of the same group and `mod name;` declarations stay on consecutive lines. It is kept within the standard formatter's `blank_lines_lower_bound` and `blank_lines_upper_bound` (0 and 1 by default), with a warning, so that the standard formatter leaves the result alone; imports and declarations get the lower bound.

In mto: supported.

generated_markers.description:
A file is generated when a comment among its first `generated_marker_line_search_limit` lines holds one of these texts. Layout leaves a generated file's items where they are unless `layout_generated_files` is set, and formatting leaves it as written when `format_generated_files = false`. A folder of generated code is better left out with `ignore_dirs`.

In mto: supported.

group_impls.description:
Rank each impl block as the struct, enum or trait it is for and place it right after that item, instead of in the `ImplBlock` group of `type_order`.

In mto: supported.

ignore_dirs.description:
Folders skipped when mto walks a directory. A name (`target`) skips every folder of that name, wherever it is; an entry with a `/` is a path (`tests/fixtures`, `./cache`, or an absolute one), read from the folder of the file that sets it, and skips that folder only. Setting this list replaces the default list.

In mto: supported.

impl_method_order.description:
The order of the functions inside an impl of a trait declared in the same file. Only the functions trade places; other items and blank lines stay where they are. A trait declared under the same name twice in the file is skipped. The standard formatter's `reorder_impl_items` is honored as well, as the standard formatter applies it.

In mto: supported.

import_grouping.description:
Separate `use` declarations into three groups, in this order, with a blank line between groups: the standard library (`std`, `core`, `alloc`), external crates, and local paths (`crate`, `self`, `super`). Only applies when `sort_imports` is on.

In mto: supported.

import_sort.description:
Imports are sorted exactly as the standard formatter sorts them, so the standard formatter leaves them alone. This picks which of the standard formatter's two orders to use when it should differ from the style edition in effect.

In mto: supported.

layout.description:
Turns layout on for the files this mto.toml applies to. Off by default, so mto moves no items until a project opts in; `mto init` writes an mto.toml with it on. An mto.toml without it may still set formatting and override the standard formatter's settings.

In mto: supported.

format.description:
Formats the files this mto.toml applies to in the Rust style, as the standard formatter does with the same settings, beside or without `layout`. On by default, so mto with no configuration is a drop-in for the standard formatter; `format = false` turns it off. Formatting changes whitespace and the few tokens the Rust style rewrites (a trailing comma, the order of imports). Like the standard formatter, it leaves as written what it would give up on: macro bodies it cannot read as code, `macro_rules!` definitions, anything marked `#[rustfmt::skip]`, `// mto: off` regions, a statement or item that cannot fit within `max_width`, and files that `disable_all_formatting` or `format_generated_files = false` leave alone. Every change is checked to keep the program's tokens and comments, and a second run changes nothing.

In mto: partial. Every construct, matching the standard formatter on the corpus (cargo xtask diff); some of its settings not yet (mto config options); what it gives up on is left as written.

layout_generated_files.description:
Whether layout reorders the items of a generated file (one holding a `generated_markers` text near its top). Off by default, so generated code keeps the order its generator wrote; formatting follows `format_generated_files` instead.

In mto: supported.

name_sort.description:
How `sort_alphabetically` compares names. Imports and modules are not affected: they are always sorted exactly as the standard formatter sorts them.

In mto: supported.

sort_alphabetically.description:
Within each kind of `type_order`, items are ordered by `visibility_order`, then by name (see `name_sort`) when this is on. When off, items of the same kind and visibility keep their original order.

In mto: supported.

sort_imports.description:
Sort `use` declarations: by group when `import_grouping` is on, then `self`, `super` and `crate` paths ahead of the rest, then by path. When off, imports keep the order they were written in; pair it with the standard formatter's `reorder_imports = false`, or the standard formatter sorts them.

In mto: supported.

test_module.description:
Where `#[cfg(test)]` modules go: last in the file, or kept where they are.

In mto: supported.

trait_impl_order.description:
Trait impls for these traits come right after the type's own impls, in this order, for example `["Default", "Clone", "Debug", "Display"]`. A trait is matched by its name without its path, so `fmt::Display` matches `Display`. Other trait impls follow, as `trait_impl_sort` says.

In mto: supported.

trait_impl_sort.description:
The impls of one type go in this order: the type's own impls, as written; the trait impls listed in `trait_impl_order`; then the other trait impls, by trait name or as written.

In mto: supported.

type_order.description:
The order in which kinds of items appear in a file, top to bottom. Kinds left out of the list go after the listed ones, in their default order. `#[cfg(test)]` modules go where `test_module` says. `extern crate` items and item macro calls (such as `include!`) are not kinds here: they never move, because moving them can change what the code means.

In mto: supported.

visibility_order.description:
Within each kind of `type_order`, items are ordered by visibility in this order before they are sorted by name. Visibilities left out go last. Modules ignore it, as the standard formatter does.

In mto: supported.

array_width.description:
Maximum width of an array literal before falling back to vertical formatting.

In mto: partial. With format = true, for the statements laid out so far (calls, chains, struct literals, arrays, tuples) and attributes.

attr_fn_like_width.description:
Maximum width of the args of a function-like attributes before falling back to vertical formatting.

In mto: supported. With format = true, for attributes.

binop_separator.description:
Where to put a binary operator when a binary expression goes multiline.

In mto: missing.

blank_lines_lower_bound.description:
Minimum number of blank lines which must be put between items. If two items have fewer blank lines between them, additional blank lines are inserted.

In mto: partial. Layout keeps the blank lines between items within it; formatting does not add blank lines yet.

blank_lines_upper_bound.description:
Maximum number of blank lines which can be put between items. If more than this number of consecutive empty lines are found, they are trimmed down to match this integer.

In mto: partial. Layout keeps the blank lines between items within it; with format = true, within blocks too.

brace_style.description:
Brace style for items

In mto: partial. With format = true, for item headers and their where clauses.

chain_width.description:
Maximum width of a chain to fit on one line.

In mto: partial. With format = true, for the statements laid out so far (calls, chains, struct literals, arrays, tuples) and attributes.

color.description:
Whether to use colored output or not.

In mto: missing.

combine_control_expr.description:
Combine control expressions with function calls.

In mto: supported. With format = true, an if, for, loop or while alone in a call does not overflow when false.

comment_width.description:
Maximum length of comments. No effect unless `wrap_comments = true`.

In mto: missing.

condense_wildcard_suffixes.description:
Replace strings of _ wildcards by a single .. in tuple patterns

In mto: missing.

control_brace_style.description:
Brace style for control flow constructs

In mto: missing.

disable_all_formatting.description:
Don't reformat anything.

Note that this option may be soft-deprecated in the future once the ignore option is stabilized. Nightly toolchain users are encouraged to use ignore instead when possible.

In mto: supported. Formatting leaves the file as written; layout follows mto.toml.

doc_comment_code_block_small_heuristics.description:
Value for `use_small_heuristics` for use in code blocks in doc comments. Only used if `format_code_in_doc_comments` is true.

In mto: missing.

doc_comment_code_block_width.description:
Max width for code snippets included in doc comments. Only used if `format_code_in_doc_comments` is true.

In mto: missing.

edition.description:
Specifies which edition is used by the parser.

In mto: partial. Read from --edition, Cargo.toml and config files; parsing still detects the edition itself.

empty_item_single_line.description:
Put empty-body functions and impls on a single line

In mto: missing.

enum_discrim_align_threshold.description:
The maximum length of enum variant having discriminant, that gets vertically aligned with others. Variants without discriminants would be ignored for the purpose of alignment.

Note that this is not how much whitespace is inserted, but instead the longest variant name that doesn't get ignored when aligning.

In mto: missing.

error_on_line_overflow.description:
Error if the formatter is unable to get all lines within `max_width`, except for comments and string literals. If this happens, then it is a bug in the formatter. You might be able to work around the bug by refactoring your code to avoid long/complex expressions, usually by extracting a local variable or using a shorter name.

In mto: missing.

error_on_unformatted.description:
Error if unable to get comments or string literals within `max_width`, or they are left with trailing whitespaces.

In mto: missing.

file_lines.description:
Lines to format; this is not supported in rustfmt.toml, and can only be specified via the --file-lines option

In mto: missing.

float_literal_trailing_zero.description:
Control the presence of trailing zero in floating-point literal values

In mto: missing.

fn_args_layout.description:
This option is deprecated and has been renamed to `fn_params_layout` to better communicate that it affects the layout of parameters in function signatures.

Deprecated: use `fn_params_layout`.

In mto: not planned. Deprecated in the standard formatter in favour of fn_params_layout.

fn_call_width.description:
Maximum width of the args of a function call before falling back to vertical formatting.

In mto: partial. With format = true, for the statements laid out so far (calls, chains, struct literals, arrays, tuples) and attributes.

fn_params_layout.description:
Control the layout of parameters in function signatures.

In mto: partial. With format = true, Tall only.

fn_single_line.description:
Put single-expression functions on a single line

In mto: missing.

force_explicit_abi.description:
Always print the abi for extern items

In mto: supported. With format = true, `extern` alone written `extern "C"` on functions, blocks and function pointer types.

force_multiline_blocks.description:
Force multiline closure and match arm bodies to be wrapped in a block

In mto: missing.

format_code_in_doc_comments.description:
Format code snippet included in doc comments.

In mto: missing.

format_generated_files.description:
Format generated files. A file is considered generated if any of the first several lines contain a `@generated` comment marker. The number of lines to check is configured by `generated_marker_line_search_limit`.

By default, generated files are reformatted, i. e. `@generated` marker is ignored. This option is currently ignored for stdin (`@generated` in stdin is ignored.)

In mto: supported. With format = true; also on stdin, which the standard formatter does not check.

format_macro_bodies.description:
Format the bodies of declarative macro definitions.

In mto: supported. With format = true: rules laid out, transcribers as written.

format_macro_matchers.description:
Format the metavariable matching patterns in macros.

In mto: missing.

format_strings.description:
Format string literals where necessary

In mto: missing.

generated_marker_line_search_limit.description:
Number of lines to check for a `@generated` pragma header, starting from the top of the file. Setting this value to `0` will treat all files as non-generated. When`format_generated_files` is `true`, this option has no effect.

In mto: supported. With format = true.

group_imports.description:
Controls the strategy for how consecutive imports are grouped together.

Controls the strategy for grouping sets of consecutive imports. Imports may contain newlines between imports and still be grouped together as a single set, but other statements between imports will result in different grouping sets.

In mto: partial. Mto.toml's import_grouping groups use items; not the standard formatter's StdExternalCrate.

hard_tabs.description:
Use tab characters for indentation, spaces for alignment

In mto: partial. With format = true, indentation uses tabs.

hex_literal_case.description:
Control the case of the letters in hexadecimal literal values

In mto: missing.

hide_parse_errors.description:
This option is deprecated and has been renamed to `show_parse_errors` to avoid confusion around the double negative default of `hide_parse_errors=false`.

In mto: not planned. Deprecated in the standard formatter in favour of show_parse_errors.

ignore.description:
Skip formatting files and directories that match the specified pattern. The pattern format is the same as .gitignore. Be sure to use Unix/forwardslash `/` style  paths. This path style will work on all platforms. Windows style paths with backslashes `\` are not supported.

In mto: partial. Mto.toml's ignore_dirs skips directories by name; no paths or globs.

imports_granularity.description:
Controls how imports are structured in `use` statements. Imports will be merged or split to the configured level of granularity.

Similar to other `import` related configuration options, this option operates within the bounds of user-defined groups of imports. See `group_imports` for more information on import groups.

Note that the formatter will not modify the granularity of imports containing comments if doing so could potentially lose or misplace said comments.

In mto: missing.

imports_indent.description:
Indent style of imports

In mto: missing.

imports_layout.description:
Item layout inside a imports block

In mto: partial. With format = true, for use declarations; Horizontal leaves a list too wide for its line as written.

indent_style.description:
Indent on expressions or items.

In mto: missing.

inline_attribute_width.description:
Write an item and its attribute on the same line if their combined width is below a threshold

In mto: missing.

make_backup.description:
Internal option, use `--backup`

In mto: not planned. Every run that writes files is recorded in history; `mto restore` undoes it.

match_arm_blocks.description:
Controls whether arm bodies are wrapped in cases where the first line of the body cannot fit on the same line as the `=>` operator.

The Style Guide requires that bodies are block wrapped by default if a line break is required after the `=>`, but this option can be used to disable that behavior to prevent wrapping arm bodies in that event, so long as the body contains neither multiple statements nor line comments.

In mto: missing.

match_arm_indent.description:
Controls whether match arms are indented.  If disabled, match arms will be formatted at the same indentation level as the outer `match` statement.  Meaning that match blocks will only be indented once, not twice.

In mto: supported. With format = true.

match_arm_leading_pipes.description:
Controls whether to include a leading pipe on match arms

In mto: supported. With format = true, for arms mto lays out.

match_block_trailing_comma.description:
Put a trailing comma after a block based match arm (non-block arms are not affected)

In mto: supported. With format = true.

max_width.description:
Maximum width of each line

In mto: partial. With format = true: lines broken and joined for the statements laid out so far, and statements too long left as written.

merge_derives.description:
Merge multiple derives into a single one.

In mto: supported. With format = true, runs of `#[derive(..)]` with no blank line or comment between them merged into one.

merge_imports.description:
This option is deprecated. Use `imports_granularity = "Crate"` instead.

Deprecated: use `imports_granularity`.

In mto: not planned. Deprecated in the standard formatter in favour of imports_granularity.

newline_style.description:
Unix or Windows line endings

In mto: supported. With format = true.

normalize_comments.description:
Convert /* */ comments to // comments where possible

In mto: missing.

normalize_doc_attributes.description:
Convert `#![doc]` and `#[doc]` attributes to `//!` and `///` doc comments.

In mto: missing.

overflow_delimited_expr.description:
When structs, slices, arrays, and block/array-like macros are used as the last argument in an expression list, allow them to overflow (like blocks/closures) instead of being indented on a new line.

In mto: missing.

print_misformatted_file_names.description:
Internal option, use `-l` or `--files-with-diff`

In mto: missing.

remove_nested_parens.description:
Remove nested parens.

In mto: supported. With format = true, parentheses directly inside parentheses dropped when no comment is among them.

reorder_impl_items.description:
Reorder impl items. `type` and `const` are put first, then macros and methods.

In mto: supported. As the standard formatter nightly applies it.

reorder_imports.description:
Reorder import and extern crate statements alphabetically in groups (a group is separated by a newline).

In mto: partial. With format = true, runs of use items sorted as the standard formatter sorts them; a run holding a comment keeps its order, and lists inside an item are not sorted yet.

reorder_modules.description:
Reorder `mod` declarations alphabetically in group.

In mto: partial. With format = true, runs of `mod name;` sorted by name; a run holding a comment keeps its order.

required_version.description:
Require a specific version of the formatter. If you want to make sure that the specific version of the formatter is used in your CI, use this option.

In mto: missing.

short_array_element_width_threshold.description:
The width threshold for an array element to be considered "short".

The layout of an array is dependent on the length of each of its elements. If the length of every element in an array is below this threshold (all elements are "short") then the array can be formatted in the mixed/compressed style, but if any one element has a length that exceeds this threshold then the array elements will have to be formatted vertically.

In mto: partial. With format = true, for the statements laid out so far (calls, chains, struct literals, arrays, tuples) and attributes.

show_parse_errors.description:
Show parse errors if the parser failed to parse files.

In mto: missing.

single_line_if_else_max_width.description:
Maximum line length for single line if-else expressions. A value of `0` (zero) results in if-else expressions always being broken into multiple lines. Note this occurs when `use_small_heuristics` is set to `Off`.

In mto: partial. With format = true, for an `if` with one-expression branches as a value or a block's tail; not yet in match arms.

single_line_let_else_max_width.description:
Maximum line length for single line let-else statements. See the let-else statement section of the Rust Style Guide for more details on when a let-else statement may be written on a single line. A value of `0` (zero) means the divergent `else` block will always be formatted over multiple lines. Note this occurs when `use_small_heuristics` is set to `Off`.

By default this option is set as a percentage of `max_width` provided by `use_small_heuristics`, but a value set directly for `single_line_let_else_max_width` will take precedence.

In mto: partial. With format = true, a `let ... else` block of one expression on the `let`'s line.

skip_children.description:
Don't reformat out of line modules

In mto: supported. The files a path's modules reach are left out, as --skip-children leaves them.

skip_macro_invocations.description:
Skip formatting the bodies of macro invocations with the following names.

The formatter will not format any macro invocation for macros with names set in this list. Including the special value "*" will prevent any macro invocations from being formatted.

Note: This option does not have any impact on how the formatter formats macro definitions.

In mto: supported. With format = true, the calls of the macros named, by their path as written, or of all for `*`, left as written.

space_after_colon.description:
Leave a space after the colon.

In mto: supported. With format = true.

space_before_colon.description:
Leave a space before the colon.

In mto: supported. With format = true.

spaces_around_ranges.description:
Put spaces around the .., ..=, and ... range operators

In mto: supported. With format = true.

struct_field_align_threshold.description:
The maximum diff of width between struct fields to be aligned with each other.

In mto: missing.

struct_lit_single_line.description:
Put small struct literals on a single line

In mto: supported. With format = true.

struct_lit_width.description:
Maximum width in the body of a struct literal before falling back to vertical formatting. A value of `0` (zero) results in struct literals always being broken into multiple lines. Note this occurs when `use_small_heuristics` is set to `Off`.

In mto: partial. With format = true, for the statements laid out so far (calls, chains, struct literals, arrays, tuples) and attributes.

struct_variant_width.description:
Maximum width in the body of a struct variant before falling back to vertical formatting. A value of `0` (zero) results in struct literals always being broken into multiple lines. Note this occurs when `use_small_heuristics` is set to `Off`.

In mto: supported. With format = true.

style_edition.description:
Controls the edition of the Rust Style Guide to use for formatting (RFC 3338)

From style edition 2024 the default is "2024".

In mto: partial. Resolved as the standard formatter resolves it and decides the defaults; import order follows it.

tab_spaces.description:
Number of spaces per tab

In mto: partial. With format = true, the width of one indentation level.

trailing_comma.description:
How to handle trailing commas for lists

In mto: partial. With format = true, for struct fields and enum variants; Never leaves a last one written with a comma as written.

trailing_semicolon.description:
Add trailing semicolon after break, continue and return

In mto: partial. With format = true, a `;` after a block's last `return`, `break` or `continue`.

type_punctuation_density.description:
Determines if `+` or `=` are wrapped in spaces in the punctuation of types

In mto: partial. With format = true, a bound's + and a type parameter's =.

unstable_features.description:
Enable unstable features on the unstable channel.

In mto: missing.

use_field_init_shorthand.description:
Use field initialize shorthand if possible.

In mto: supported. With format = true.

use_small_heuristics.description:
This option can be used to simplify the management and bulk updates of the granular width configuration settings (`fn_call_width`, `attr_fn_like_width`, `struct_lit_width`, `struct_variant_width`, `array_width`, `chain_width`, `single_line_if_else_max_width`), that respectively control when formatted constructs are multi-lined/vertical based on width.

Note that explicitly provided values for the width configuration settings take precedence and override the calculated values determined by `use_small_heuristics`.

In mto: partial. With format = true, for the statements laid out so far (calls, chains, struct literals, arrays, tuples) and attributes.

use_try_shorthand.description:
Replace uses of the try! macro by the ? shorthand

In mto: missing.

verbose.description:
How much to information to emit to the user

In mto: missing.

version.description:
This option is deprecated and has been replaced by `style_edition`. `version = "One"` is equivalent to `style_edition = "(2015|2018|2021)"` and `version = "Two"` is equivalent to `style_edition = "2024"`

From style edition 2024 the default is "Two".

In mto: partial. Deprecated in the standard formatter; `Two` means style edition 2024, as in the standard formatter.

where_single_line.description:
Forces the `where` clause to be laid out on a single line.

In mto: missing.

wrap_comments.description:
Break comments to fit on the line

Note that no wrapping will happen if:
1. The comment is the start of a markdown header doc comment
2. A URL was found in the comment

In mto: missing.
